title: Lincoln boss Tom Shaw set for first Wrexham clash since captaining Chester

It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Tom Shaw is set to face Wrexham for the first time as a manager having come up against The Reds on four occasions whilst captain of Chester. The former Seals midfielder scored against The Reds at The Deva Stadium in October 2015, before wearing the armband in his final two derby appearances. Shaw's goal came in a 3-2 win over a Wrexham side that would finish eighth under Gary Mills in the National League. Mills' team got their revenge with a 3-0 home victory that March though, before both teams cancelled each other out the following season. Shaw then missed The Reds' 1-0 away win in 2017 and left for Tamworth in the January, as Chester were relegated from the fifth tier at the end of the campaign. Wrexham 0 Chester 0, 2017- Tom Shaw goes down from Hamza Bencherif tackle but his appeals are waived away, RM240916b (Image: Newsquest) Read more Wrexham boss gives Kieffer Moore and Issa Kabore injury update Lewis O'Brien backs Wrexham to build momentum after international break 'Calming influence' Joe Worrall relishing Wrexham captaincy role The Lincoln co-manager also operated as a coach during his time in Cheshire despite being 29 upon his arrival, and joined Lincoln's academy set up at the end of the 2017/18 season. The 39-year-old has since progressed through the club's coaching set-up and landed the job as first team boss alongside Chris Cohen in May, after Michael Skubala left to manage Bristol City. The pair were nominated for September's Manager of the Month award, but have since watched their side drop to 21st in the table after six defeats in their last eight games.
